main_body: A 64x48 flat ground patch, dark mossy green with small repeating tufts and red and yellow dots. It is not a standing object.
top_band: none: the column scan shows one uniform run (rows 0-47, L about 49-51) with no top band or front face. This is flat terrain, so the 3/4 contract does not apply.
evidence: The drawing is a seamless ground texture with no object volume, so none of the four failure modes (front elevation, side elevation, top-down slab, rim only) applies. Terrain is meant to be flat.

style.evidence: The candidate has 12 distinct colours and a median of 12 per tile. The grass reference has 80 colours and a median of 26, so the candidate is well below it, though it is above the paving reference (7 and 7). The dark edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so the darker clumps lean green rather than black. The base is a near-uniform dark green with only subtle noise, about 4 value steps against the grass reference's 5-6. Detail comes from sparse tufts and dots that repeat identically on a 16px grid, which reads as a mechanical stamp rather than hand-varied grass clumps. It is thinner and more repetitive than the grass reference, so I fail it under the strict standard.
